plain: How much memory the game makes the browser use, second by second, from launch to the results screen. Each line is one run.

charts.title: Safari on a 16 GB Mac mini: main vs v0.5.0
charts.caption: Safari stops the game's page when its WebContent process gets too big: at 8,473 MB and 8,793 MB in these runs. Both runs where the kong moved around were stopped: main 55 seconds after landing, and v0.5.0 before it had even landed. The run where the kong stood still lasted to the results screen at 8,049 MB. Each step up is a new location loading, and nothing is released afterwards.
charts.killLabel: Safari stopped the page at 8,793 MB

charts.title: Chrome vs Safari on the same 16 GB Mac mini
charts.caption: Both runs leave the kong standing still. Chrome levels off at about 10 GB for the whole browser (9,943 MB median 60 seconds into a match, six runs) and doesn't grow in a second match. Safari keeps climbing as locations load and reaches 9,278 MB by the results screen. Chrome's total counts every browser process. Safari's counts only the page's process and its graphics process, so Safari's real total is higher than shown. The two runs are on different builds: main 7890f3b for Chrome, main f417032 for Safari. The Chrome run ends at 320 seconds. It plays two matches and leaves each one about 60 seconds after landing (the first runs from Play at 34 seconds to leaving at 178 seconds). It doesn't play a match through to the results screen, so it doesn't show Chrome over a full match.
charts.note: Swap and memory pressure (Chrome runs 4 to 6): about 2.5 GB of swap was already in use before each run, and it never rose during one (peaks of 2,571, 2,539 and 2,499 MB, each the starting value). macOS reported memory pressure as "warn" at every sample and never "critical".
charts.source: project drive: handoffs/memory-baseline-metal-v3/README.md (medians, swap, pressure) and handoffs/safari-growth/README.md

charts.title: Low-memory mode on vs off (Chrome on Windows, D3D11)
charts.caption: Low-memory mode (?lowmem=1) waits to build each location until the player gets near it, but it never unloads one. It only saves memory early on: in the plane it held about 7,100 MB against about 13,300 MB with it off. Memory climbs from the moment the kong lands. After about 2 km travelled (the plane, the drop and one leg of walking) it already holds 21 of the 26 locations, and by 4 km the two lines have met (about 14,200 MB against 13,700 MB). Both runs end at about 13,300 MB on the results screen, and the peak is only about 200 MB lower with it on. These runs used the older measuring script. On this Windows machine the fixed script gave the same totals as the older one, so the numbers hold.
charts.source: project drive: handoffs/lowmem-growth-d3d11/README.md (distance table, module counts) and cdp/samples.csv, cdp/*/growth.json (plane-phase samples) (RAY-122); the overstatement is KONG-43; v3 confirmation for D3D11: project drive handoffs/memory-baseline-d3d11-v3/README.md (RAY-130)

charts.title: Chrome on Windows (D3D11) with the fixed measuring script: main vs v0.4.1
charts.caption: Three runs of each build with the fixed measuring script, both standing still. At every measured phase, main 7890f3b's median was lower: 6,091 MB against 8,063 MB at the title, 12,364 MB against 12,718 MB thirty seconds into a match, and 12,631 MB against 12,812 MB after leaving the second match. The chart shows one run of each, and between those phases the two lines sometimes cross. The two builds don't run at the same quality, though. Since #125, main boots at high on Auto on this machine, while v0.4.1 boots at ultra, and that change accounts for most of the gap at the title.
charts.source: project drive: handoffs/memory-baseline-d3d11-v3/README.md (medians, quality tiers) and main-1, v041-1 result.json (RAY-130); the chart shows run 1 of each

charts.title: Chrome on Windows (D3D11): v0.4.0 vs v0.4.1
charts.caption: The release measurements found v0.4.1 used 469 MB less than v0.4.0 thirty seconds into a match (13,188 to 12,719 MB, median of three runs each). These runs used the older measuring script, which overstated totals on the Mac. Rerunning v0.4.1 with the fixed script gave 12,718 MB at the same point, against 12,764 MB from the older script, so these Windows numbers hold.
charts.source: project drive: handoffs/release-kong-v0.4.1-d3d11/README.md (medians) and memory/runs/*/result.json; the overstatement is KONG-43; v3 confirmation: project drive handoffs/memory-baseline-d3d11-v3/README.md (RAY-130)
